findings.classification: conditional design-gap candidate; static only; no confirmed Gateway authorization bypass
findings.title: Device revocation does not synchronously invalidate the Linux helper's cached bearer
findings.severity: Low if Gateway-side rejection is the contract; higher only if local bearer delivery must stop immediately
findings.trigger: A device is revoked after managed-linux.py has fetched a device-bound access token and before its next successful service loop. A process running as the enrolled UID connects to the local Unix socket during the remaining cache lifetime.

static_evidence.evidence: The local socket authorizes only by SO_PEERCRED UID and cache.until; it does not consult device status, activation, or a revocation signal before returning the cached Authorization header.

An active compliant heartbeat fetches a bearer, caches it for 120 seconds, and then selects a 60-second pause. The observer work follows token fetch and can take up to two 40-second subprocess timeouts.
Cache is cleared when the next loop detects an error, not when the remote admin invokes revocation.
Revocation sets endpoint_agents.status='revoked' and records an event; there is no local push/channel to the Linux service.
Subsequent device-key requests require status='active', so the next managed-policy/token request is rejected after revocation.
Fresh token minting re-authenticates the device and invokes managed_failure before issuing a five-minute token.
Device-bound access checks re-read current device status, owner_token, managed_state, device_epoch, heartbeat freshness, and policy hash.
The user/MCP contract checks call managed_failure before the request proceeds.
The protocol dispatch path also blocks on managed_failure before policy/dispatch.

findings.expected_control: If revocation semantics include immediate local credential non-delivery, the socket should stop returning a bearer as soon as revocation is committed. Existing Gateway-side checks appear to stop protected use after the DB status changes.
findings.reproducible_static_scenario: With synthetic endpoint/principal records only: establish active+compliant state and a cached token; apply endpoint status=revoked; request a header from the same enrolled UID before cache.until; separately trace the same token through the Gateway auth/dispatch checks. Expected source-derived result: local helper can return the cached header while Gateway-managed_failure rejects protected use. This scenario was not executed.
normal_cases: Active endpoint, exact enrolled UID, unexpired cache: helper returns Authorization; Gateway accepts only if current DB state and policy remain valid.
Active endpoint, wrong UID: SO_PEERCRED check returns activation-required error and no Authorization header.
boundary_cases: Revocation immediately after a token fetch: same-UID local helper may still return that bearer until its cache expiry or next loop error clears the cache; the upper cache bound from fetch is 120 seconds, with service polling cadence/observer delays affecting detection timing.

Same UID is the local principal boundary: any process under that UID can request the helper's bearer, regardless of process identity. Socket mode 0600 and SO_PEERCRED UID do not provide per-process separation; this is a design boundary, not a demonstrated cross-user bypass.

A request handler that copied the token under the lock may send it after a concurrent cache.clear(); the send is outside the lock. This is a narrow local delivery race; Gateway-side authorization still must be evaluated independently.
findings.fix_direction_for_later_review: Decide and document whether endpoint revocation promises immediate helper-side bearer withdrawal or only Gateway-side denial. If immediate local withdrawal is required, use a revocation/lease design with a bounded and explicit stale window; a periodic heartbeat alone cannot provide instantaneous local invalidation. Preserve a no-network/no-database local helper path if required by the trust model, and keep Gateway authorization checks as the authoritative backstop.

validation_plan_not_run.positive: Synthetic DB: active device, matching principal/device_epoch/device_policy, recent heartbeat; local helper returns header and Gateway accepts only valid request.
validation_plan_not_run.negative: Revoke device then request at the local socket and at Gateway; record helper response and independently assert Gateway auth denial/no dispatch.
validation_plan_not_run.boundary: Run local requests at revoke+0, revoke+TTL-ε, revoke+TTL+ε; race cache.clear against one socket handler; assert no Gateway effect from stale token.
validation_plan_not_run.evidence_required: Separate DB transaction timestamps, helper socket response class (never bearer value), Gateway HTTP/auth result, decision/dispatch ledger, monotonic cache expiry, and source revision. Use synthetic tokens/data only.

findings.status: static_source_inference_only; no unit test, DB-preserving run, isolated DB test, local socket probe, or kernel evidence performed

scenario_matrix.condition: Active+compliant device, fresh heartbeat, current policy, correct enrolled UID
scenario_matrix.expected: Cached local header may be returned; current Gateway principal/device/epoch/policy checks permit the request.

scenario_matrix.condition: Wrong local UID connects to token socket
scenario_matrix.expected: No Authorization header; helper returns activation-required error.

scenario_matrix.condition: Admin revokes device while previously cached token remains unexpired
scenario_matrix.expected: Local helper may deliver stale bearer until local expiry/next failed poll; fresh mint and Gateway protected use should fail based on revoked status.

scenario_matrix.condition: Header handler copies token while service thread clears cache after a failure
scenario_matrix.expected: One copied response can still be sent; evaluate as stale local delivery only, then assert Gateway denies it.

scenario_matrix.condition: Admin activates a recently compliant device using displayed expected policy hash
scenario_matrix.expected: CAS update requires active device, current policy hash, recent heartbeat, exact config hashes, and every platform check true; owner cannot activate own device.

scenario_matrix.condition: Stale/mismatched policy hash, stale heartbeat, or any missing/false check
scenario_matrix.expected: Activation update affects no row and returns conflict.

control_flow_notes: LOCAL-RISK-08's intended chain is present in source: managed-linux checks health, endpoint_plane.heartbeat quarantines noncompliant devices without self-reactivation, the Linux loop clears cache for non-active/noncompliant reports, activate_managed requires an independent admin action, and managed_failure gates mint/use paths.

heartbeat() writes a fresh heartbeat timestamp even when noncompliant but sets/retains managed_state as quarantined; activate_managed() independently checks a recent heartbeat, current policy hash, exact configuration hashes, and all true required checks.

consume_enrollment() binds owner token, endpoint ID, device_epoch, local username/UID and sets the principal's managed_required flag transactionally; managed_failure() checks owner_token against the authenticated principal and validates epoch/policy.

revoke_device() changes device status. Device token minting rejects inactive status; protected resource-side paths shown above re-read device status. Local cache delivery is a distinct boundary from Gateway authorization.
limitations: The stale bearer candidate is conditional on the desired contract: Gateway-side denial is evident in the inspected source; immediate local helper withdrawal is not implemented. No successful MCP tool execution with a revoked token is evidenced.

The source audit cannot establish deployed code equality, DB isolation/transaction timing, systemd scheduling, actual SO_PEERCRED behavior, AppArmor attachment, nftables enforcement, or the measured duration of the stale-delivery window.
No changes were made to managed-linux.py, enforce-linux.py, endpoint_plane.py, or any other implementation file. No tests or environment/system changes were performed.
